_method: primary sources fetched live (gov.uk NMW rates page, Low Pay Commission remit/report pages); every figure carries a verbatim quote in source.quote

entries.title: National Living Wage £12.71 from 1 April 2026
entries.fact: The National Living Wage for workers aged 21 and over rose from £12.21 to £12.71 per hour on 1 April 2026.

quantification.how: (£12.71 − £12.21) = £0.50/hour increase × 37.5h × 52wk = £975 per full-time 21+ hourly employee per year

source.quote: The rates change on 1 April every year. Current rates [table]: 21 and over — £12.71; 18 to 20 — £10.85; Under 18 — £8; Apprentice — £8. Rates between 1 April 2024 and 31 March 2026 [table]: April 2025 to March 2026 — £12.21 (21 and over)

entries.angle: Since 1 April 2026 every 21+ hourly employee on the National Living Wage costs roughly £975 more per year in base pay than under the April 2025 rate — multiplied across a multi-site rota, a 10-site group with 15 full-time-equivalent NLW staff per site is absorbing around £146k of new annual wage cost from this step alone.
entries.proof_pairing: Customer proof showing labour cost as a % of revenue held or reduced (e.g. labour-cost-percentage improvement across sites) despite statutory wage increases.
entries.caveats: The £975 figure assumes a 37.5-hour week, 52 weeks, and an employee previously paid exactly the old NLW; staff already paid above £12.71 are unaffected directly (though pay-differential compression is common, that effect is not in the arithmetic). Applies UK-wide only — Ireland has a separate National Minimum Wage not covered by this entry.

entries.title: 18-20 rate £10.85 from 1 April 2026 (age-band convergence)
entries.fact: The National Minimum Wage for 18 to 20 year olds rose from £10.00 to £10.85 per hour on 1 April 2026, and the government has committed to lowering the National Living Wage's age of eligibility from 21 to 18 over time.

quantification.how: (£10.85 − £10.00) = £0.85/hour increase × 37.5h × 52wk = £1,657.50 per full-time 18-20 employee per year

source.quote: Current rates [table]: 18 to 20 — £10.85 ... April 2025 to March 2026 — £10 (18 to 20). [Corroborating, Low Pay Commission, gov.uk/government/publications/the-national-minimum-wage-in-2026: the remit] repeats the Government's commitment to lowering the NLW's age of eligibility from 21 to 18

entries.angle: Hospitality groups that staff heavily with 18-20 year olds took a larger proportional hit than the headline NLW step: the youth rate rose £0.85/hour on 1 April 2026 (about £1,657 per full-time 18-20 employee per year), and the government's stated commitment to align the 18-20 rate with the adult rate means this band will keep rising faster than the NLW.
entries.proof_pairing: Customer proof on scheduling/forecasting accuracy reducing over-rostered hours, expressed as labour hours or labour-cost % saved.
entries.caveats: Assumes 37.5h × 52wk full-time equivalent; many 18-20 hospitality staff are part-time, so scale to actual hours. The pace of 18-20/NLW alignment is not fixed — the Low Pay Commission has flexibility on timing, so do not state a date for full alignment.

entries.title: LPC projected NLW range £13.02–£13.34 for April 2027
entries.fact: The Low Pay Commission projects the April 2027 National Living Wage will fall in the range £13.02 to £13.34, with a central estimate of £13.18; it has been asked to recommend the April 2027 rates and its 2026 consultation closed on 26 June 2026, with no rate yet confirmed by government.

quantification.how: central estimate only: (£13.18 − £12.71) = £0.47/hour × 37.5h × 52wk = £916.50 per full-time NLW employee per year; the projected range implies £604.50 (at £13.02) to £1,228.50 (at £13.34)

source.quote: Based on current wage forecasts, we expect the rate needed to stay at two-thirds of median hourly earnings will be in the range of £13.02 and £13.34, with a central estimate of £13.18.

entries.angle: For budgeting conversations from autumn 2026: the Low Pay Commission's own published projection puts the April 2027 NLW at £13.02–£13.34 (central £13.18), i.e. roughly another £900 per full-time minimum-wage employee per year on the central estimate — a dated, sourced forward number a finance lead can plug into next year's labour budget.
entries.proof_pairing: Customer proof on forecasting-led labour budgeting (labour cost % vs budget) — pairing a projected cost with a planning capability.
entries.caveats: PROJECTION ONLY — this is the LPC's forecast of the two-thirds-of-median-earnings path, not a recommendation or a government decision; the final rate is normally announced at the Autumn Budget (November 2026). Never present £13.18 as a confirmed rate. Re-verify after the LPC recommendation and Budget announcement.
